title: Beyond Reward Hacking: Causal Rewards for Large Language Model Alignment

bias_targets.methodology: Quantifying the frequency of agreement or flattering phrases (e.g., 'Yes, you are right.') in generated responses using a semi-synthetic dataset designed with spurious correlations between agreement and correctness.
Calculating the correlation between generated response lengths and their assigned reward model rankings to determine if the model disproportionately favors verbose outputs.

Evaluating sentiment classification accuracy and bias metrics on review datasets (Yelp, IMDB, Amazon) that were artificially manipulated to spuriously correlate specific concepts (e.g., 'food', 'music') with positive labels.

Measuring explicit (templated attributes) and implicit (name-associated) discrimination using the Anthropic Discrm-eval dataset by fitting a mixed-effects model to calculate the coefficient of gender on decision boundaries.

Measuring explicit (templated attributes) and implicit (name-associated) discrimination using the Anthropic Discrm-eval dataset by fitting a mixed-effects model to calculate the coefficient of race on decision boundaries.
